prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Hi, I am looking for a cheap bottle of wine that is a little sweet with some vanilla, but still tastes fresh and crisp."

List A:
Wine 1: Pinot Grigio, Italy, $9. Tasting note: "This inexpensive, delicious fresh wine has good depth of concentration and long, vanilla flavors."
Wine 2: Chardonnay, France, $13. Tasting note: "This is a crisp, lively and fruity wine, bright with acidity and lightly textured. A vanilla edge adds extra interest. Drink now."
Wine 3: Pinot Grigio, US, $19. Tasting note: "At the equivalent of $4.75 a bottle, and with the staying power of its vacuum technology, this box wine is a pretty good buy. Bone dry and crisp, it has pleasant citrus fruit, vanilla and peppery spice flavors."
Wine 4: Cabernet Sauvignon, Australia, $20. Tasting note: "For $20, you could do a lot worse than to sample this wine, which boasts plenty of varietal character and ample quality. Cedar, tobacco, cassis and dark chocolate suggest a fully ripe wine, while the the structure remains fine and linear, with gentle, cocoa-powder-textured tannins that line the finish. Drink now–2025."
Wine 5: Chardonnay, US, $13. Tasting note: "With apricot, orange, honey, butter cream and vanilla flavors, it's a simple wine at a fair price."

List B:
Wine 1: Arinto, Portugal, $9. Tasting note: "Fresh and crisp, this is a wine that has little flavor and only the thinest palate. It is bright to drink now."
Wine 2: Melon, France, $11. Tasting note: "Soft, fruity and lightly crisp, this is a wine to drink young to keep its freshness. It has perfumed acidity and a lightly zesty lemon aftertaste."
Wine 3: Portuguese White, Portugal, $5. Tasting note: "A sweet, soft, clean wine, anonymous almost. Yes, there is freshness, lightness, but all the time the awkward, unbalancing sweetness pulls it down. Drink very chilled."
Wine 4: Chardonnay, France, $18. Tasting note: "A soft, simple and attractively fresh wine, this is ready to drink. It has all the crisp acidity you could want alongside riper yellow fruits and a soft, gentle texture. Drink now."
Wine 5: Pinot Grigio, US, $14. Tasting note: "Good for simple everyday drinking, this wine is slightly sweet but crisp with delicate citrus, peach, vanilla and honey flavors."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
